proposed_comments.title: Distinguish invalid initials protocols from transient renderer failures
proposed_comments.body:
### Distinguish invalid initials protocols from transient renderer failures

**Severity:** `high`

The generated-initials path should reject malformed protocol data without converting renderer or device failures into a cached permanent fallback. A transient `Win2D`/font/device failure can recover on a later attempt, so caching that failure leaves a stale fallback in the icon pipeline and prevents retry. Please keep parser-level invalid-input handling separate from renderer exceptions, propagate transient rendering failures to the retry-aware caller, and add regression coverage for both cases.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The behavior spans protocol parsing, renderer failure propagation, cache policy, and tests; no single current RIGHT-side diff range safely expresses the coordinated change.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The behavior spans protocol parsing, renderer failure propagation, cache policy, and tests; no single current RIGHT-side diff range safely expresses the coordinated change.

confidence.rationale: The converged fork loop added separate handling for malformed UTF-16/protocol input and transient initials-renderer failures, while the exact upstream head still contains the single failure path.

proposed_comments.title: Do not permanently cache recoverable initials rendering failures
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not permanently cache recoverable initials rendering failures

**Severity:** `high`

When initials rendering fails because the current graphics or font environment is temporarily unavailable, the failure should remain retryable instead of being materialized as a durable negative result. Otherwise an icon that could render after the environment recovers stays on the fallback path for the lifetime of the cached source. Please preserve the existing fallback for genuinely invalid protocols while allowing transient renderer failures to reach the retry path, with a regression test that exercises a failed attempt followed by a successful retry.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The required cache and retry semantics involve multiple icon-loader layers and a stateful test sequence, so this cannot be represented safely by one localized current diff suggestion.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The required cache and retry semantics involve multiple icon-loader layers and a stateful test sequence, so this cannot be represented safely by one localized current diff suggestion.

confidence.rationale: The fork review branch specifically changed negative-result caching and transient-failure propagation, and the exact upstream head validation confirms those changes are fork-only.

proposed_comments.title: Keep generated-initials tests independent of the graphics environment
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep generated-initials tests independent of the graphics environment

**Severity:** `medium`

The generated-initials protocol tests should verify the path and protocol behavior without depending on installed fonts, Win2D device state, or an interactive graphics environment. Inject the deterministic initials-path generation used by the test seam, and retain a separate production-rendering path for end-to-end behavior. This keeps the unit suite stable while still covering the real renderer failure and retry behavior in focused tests.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This is a coordinated test-seam and production-path change across the protocol implementation and unit tests, not a safe one-hunk replacement.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: This is a coordinated test-seam and production-path change across the protocol implementation and unit tests, not a safe one-hunk replacement.
